key_insight: Human experts and LLMs performed similarly in proposing synthesis recipes, and their closed-loop collaboration enabled discovery of a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that combining LLM-generated planning with lab validation can accelerate materials synthesis and expand discovery into underexplored structural spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes with both humans and an LLM for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials.
Tested recipe success through in-lab experimentation in a closed-loop workflow.
Fed experimental outcomes back to humans and LLMs for a second collaboration round.
evidence_signal: Recipe success was quantitatively evaluated by experimental outcomes, with reported success rates such as 83% vs 75% for known materials in round one and 17% vs 22% for unknown materials in round one.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply on unknown targets, so broader deployment still depends on reliable generalization beyond well-studied materials families.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
